newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips sees better chips performance in 97.
newsitem.headline: Philips sees better chips performance in 97.

text.p: Philips Electronics said on Thursday the outlook for the chip market had brightened and its semiconductors activities expected to show an improved performance in 1997.
"We look forward to a somewhat better year in 1997 than in 1996," finance director Dudley Eustace told a news conference on the company's 1996 results.
"It would appear that the pundits are rather more confident now that the bottom has been passed (in the semiconducor market)," Eustace said.
"Our own position in this is a strong order position, (with) a book-to-bill ratio...above one."
Philips Semi-conductors chairman Arthur van der Poel said in a statement the unit had managed to buck the overall decline in the chip market, posting moderate nominal growth of six percent.
"Since we do not sell memory products, we were able to show positive though moderate nominal growth of six percent (in dollar terms one percent)," the statement said.
However, increased price pressures had eroded prices by some eight percent, the statement said, while lower sales growth led to underutilisation of capacity.
As a result income from operations had fallen year-on-year, the statement said.
Philips earlier reported income from operations (excluding restructuring) at its components and semiconductors division fell to 1.59 billion guilders in 1996 from a year-earlier 2.23 billion.
Philips does not manufacture memory chips or microprocessors, but commands a 3.2 percent market share in the applications chips segment.
